item.title: Braun admin proposes tolls on I-70 to pay for highway widening
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun’s administration has proposed charging $15.60 in tolls to drive a car across Indiana on Interstate 70 in order to pay for widening all of that highway to six lanes.

item.title: City officials unveil plan to keep young people safe over spring break, including 'Connection Center'
item.description: City leaders say their plan to keep Indianapolis safe for young people focuses on curfew enforcement and providing community resources.

item.title: IPS board member Gayle Cosby resigns, citing health challenges
item.description: The announcement at a Tuesday meeting comes as substantial changes for IPS are on the horizon that will dilute the elected school board’s power.

item.title: Following targeted threats, Indiana lawmakers unite to pass doxxing bill
item.description: The legislation classifies doxxing as a threat if the intent is to cause bodily harm to a person, damage to their property, or to encourage others to commit a crime against them.

item.title: State quietly scraps plans for expanded White River State Park
item.description: State officials are abandoning plans to expand the White River State Park, Mirror Indy has learned.

item.title: TSA agents quitting in Indianapolis after latest federal shutdown
item.description: The local TSA union said some members are leaving for other work over the latest federal shutdown. Indianapolis Airport Officials said travelers won’t experience delays flying out of IND.

item.title: Multiple tornadoes barrel through Illinois and Northwest Indiana, causing at least two deaths
item.description: The tornadoes caused significant damage and injuries along the path through Illinois and Indiana.

item.title: New citizens look forward to civic life after Carmel naturalization ceremony
item.description: More than 200 people from 48 countries were sworn in as U.S. citizens during a naturalization ceremony in Carmel, with the vast majority immediately registering to vote.

item.title: Braun pushes for Christian-aligned Turning Point USA clubs in Indiana schools
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun announced a partnership with Turning Point USA on Thursday, urging colleges and high schools to bring clubs to their campuses.

item.title: Ballard to run under 'Lincoln Party' name in independent bid for Indiana secretary of state
item.description: Former Indianapolis Mayor Greg Ballard announced Wednesday that his independent campaign for Indiana secretary of state will use a “Lincoln Party” label as part of an effort that could eventually establish a new political party in the state.
